prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a buy-to-let flat. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When the property is a buy-to-let flat, I check the lease terms early, because short leases, onerous ground rent clauses, or restrictions on letting can change the case from straightforward to unsuitable very quickly."},{"type":"fact","content":"When rental income is used to support affordability, I look for a sensible stress test rather than relying on the current rent alone, because higher rates and void periods need to be covered in the assessment."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a flat sits in a block with multiple owners, I pay close attention to service charges and any planned major works, because these costs can affect both affordability and the property’s saleability."},{"type":"preference","content":"When documents are incomplete, I prefer to pause and request the tenancy agreement, latest rent evidence, and building insurance details together, because piecemeal requests slow the case down and create avoidable back-and-forth."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the applicant has several buy-to-let properties, I look for a simple portfolio pattern rather than treating each one in isolation, because arrears, vacancies, and concentration risk matter across the whole picture."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the flat is above commercial premises or in a high-rise block, I check the building’s insurance and any lending restrictions carefully, because construction type and fire-safety issues can affect whether we can proceed."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the rent looks strong but the flat has been recently renovated, I verify that the works are complete and lawful, because unfinished or non-compliant alterations can weaken the security."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the application is a remortgage, I like to see a clear reason for the switch and no unusual recent borrowing, because unexplained capital raising can indicate a different risk than a simple rate switch."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the tenancy is on a short-term or rolling basis, I treat the income as less certain than a long fixed tenancy, because turnover and voids are more likely in those cases."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the valuation comes back below the expected level, I rework the loan-to-value and rent cover immediately, because a small shift in value can quickly change the underwriting outcome on a flat."}]}
